text.p: Montserrat eased its volcano alert on Tuesday, allowing people daytime access to the capital, Plymouth, at the south end of the island and other areas in the shadow of the rumbling Soufriere Hills volcano.

It was the first time in several months that people evacuated from "unsafe zones" were allowed to visit homes and businesses abandoned last April, when authorities ordered the entire southern end of the island cleared.
Residents still will not be allowed to stay in the danger zones at night.

"The volcano activity has been stable for about two or three weeks now. We're happy that it's in a stable pattern and we can relax slightly," said Angus Miller, deputy chief scientist at the Montserrat Volcano Observatory.
Montserrat, a British colony in the eastern Caribbean, has been plagued by the volcano since it roared to life on July 18, 1995. The last time it was similarly active was 350 to 400 years ago.
